# Distributions

Values from the Bernoulli, exponential, normal, binomial, Poisson, gamma and beta distributions.

<h2 id="binomial"><code>Binomial&lt;G&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Binomial<G: RandomGenerator>(generator: &var G, trials: uint64, probability: float64) -> uint64
```

The number of successes in `trials` independent trials each succeeding with probability `probability`.
A probability at or below zero gives zero successes and one at or above one gives every trial, matching
[`Bernoulli`](/docs/api/random/distributions#bernoulli)'s treatment of the same edges. Zero trials give zero.
Small counts are summed directly, which is the definition. Large ones are split by a beta draw: the median
trial's success probability has a beta distribution, and comparing it to `probability` says which side the
answer falls on and leaves a strictly smaller problem. That halves the count each step, so a binomial over a
billion trials costs about thirty draws rather than a billion.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Random/Src/Counting.rux#L21)

**Type parameters**

| Name                 | Description          |
| -------------------- | -------------------- |
| `G: RandomGenerator` | the generator's type |

**Parameters**

| Name          | Type      | Description                        |
| ------------- | --------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `generator`   | `&var G`  | where the bits come from           |
| `trials`      | `uint64`  | how many independent trials        |
| `probability` | `float64` | the chance of success, in `[0, 1]` |

**Returns**: how many of `trials` succeeded

<h2 id="poisson"><code>Poisson&lt;G&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Poisson<G: RandomGenerator>(generator: &var G, mean: float64) -> uint64
```

The number of events in one interval when they arrive independently at the given mean rate.
A mean at or below zero gives zero. A small mean uses Knuth's method — multiply uniforms until the product
falls below `exp(-mean)` — which costs about `mean` draws and is exact. A large mean would cost too many
draws that way, and the product would underflow to zero before the loop ended, so the mean is consumed in
chunks: a gamma draw of integer shape is the waiting time for that many events, and either it overshoots the
interval, in which case the count is a binomial of what is left, or it fits and the remainder carries on.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Random/Src/Counting.rux#L54)

**Type parameters**

| Name                 | Description          |
| -------------------- | -------------------- |
| `G: RandomGenerator` | the generator's type |

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type      | Description              |
| ----------- | --------- | ------------------------ |
| `generator` | `&var G`  | where the bits come from |
| `mean`      | `float64` | the distribution's mean  |

**Returns**: a draw from the Poisson distribution with that mean

<h2 id="bernoulli"><code>Bernoulli&lt;G&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Bernoulli<G: RandomGenerator>(generator: &var G, probability: float64) -> bool
```

A coin that comes up `true` with probability `probability`.
A probability at or below zero never comes up true and one at or above one always does, so a caller
computing a probability that drifts slightly out of range gets the sensible answer rather than an
occasional inversion. The comparison is against a draw in `[0, 1)`, so a probability of exactly zero is
impossible rather than merely rare — which is what makes the two ends behave.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Random/Src/Distribution.rux#L19)

**Type parameters**

| Name                 | Description          |
| -------------------- | -------------------- |
| `G: RandomGenerator` | the generator's type |

**Parameters**

| Name          | Type      | Description                        |
| ------------- | --------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `generator`   | `&var G`  | where the bits come from           |
| `probability` | `float64` | the chance of success, in `[0, 1]` |

**Returns**: true with the given probability

<h2 id="exponential"><code>Exponential&lt;G&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Exponential<G: RandomGenerator>(generator: &var G) -> float64
```

A value from the exponential distribution with rate one.
The inverse-transform method: the negated logarithm of a uniform draw. Written on `1 - u` rather than on `u`
because [`NextFloat64`](/docs/api/random/random-generator#next-float64) can return exactly zero, whose logarithm is an infinity — so the draw that would
produce an infinite sample is instead the one that produces zero, which the distribution does allow.
Multiply the result by a mean, or divide by a rate, to scale it.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Random/Src/Distribution.rux#L34)

**Type parameters**

| Name                 | Description          |
| -------------------- | -------------------- |
| `G: RandomGenerator` | the generator's type |

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type     | Description              |
| ----------- | -------- | ------------------------ |
| `generator` | `&var G` | where the bits come from |

**Returns**: a draw from the exponential distribution with rate one

<h2 id="exponential-with-rate"><code>ExponentialWithRate&lt;G&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func ExponentialWithRate<G: RandomGenerator>(generator: &var G, rate: float64) -> float64
```

A value from the exponential distribution with the given rate.
A rate at or below zero has no distribution and gives zero.

<h2 id="normal-pair"><code>NormalPair&lt;G&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func NormalPair<G: RandomGenerator>(generator: &var G, first: *var float64, second: *var float64)
```

A pair of independent standard normal values.
The Box-Muller transform, which produces two at a time from two uniform draws — so this returns both rather
than throwing one away. The radial draw is taken on `1 - u` for the same reason as the exponential: the
logarithm of an exact zero is an infinity, and the generator will produce an exact zero eventually.
The polar form of the transform avoids the trigonometric functions at the cost of rejecting about a fifth of
its draws; this uses the direct form, which consumes a fixed two words and is therefore reproducible in a way
a rejection loop is not.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Random/Src/Distribution.rux#L62)

**Type parameters**

| Name                 | Description          |
| -------------------- | -------------------- |
| `G: RandomGenerator` | the generator's type |

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type           | Description                          |
| ----------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `generator` | `&var G`       | where the bits come from             |
| `first`     | `*var float64` | receives the first of the two draws  |
| `second`    | `*var float64` | receives the second of the two draws |

<h2 id="normal"><code>Normal&lt;G&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Normal<G: RandomGenerator>(generator: &var G) -> float64
```

A single standard normal value: mean zero, standard deviation one.
Discards the second value of the pair. A caller drawing many should use [`NormalPair`](/docs/api/random/distributions#normal-pair) and keep both, which
halves the work.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Random/Src/Distribution.rux#L76)

| ----------- | -------- | ------------------------ |
| `generator` | `&var G` | where the bits come from |

**Returns**: a draw from the standard normal distribution

<h2 id="normal-with"><code>NormalWith&lt;G&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func NormalWith<G: RandomGenerator>(generator: &var G, mean: float64, deviation: float64) -> float64
```

A normal value with the given mean and standard deviation.
A negative standard deviation is reflected rather than refused, since the distribution it describes is the
same one; a zero gives the mean exactly.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Random/Src/Distribution.rux#L92)

<h2 id="direct-method-limit"><code>DirectMethodLimit</code></h2>

```rux
pub const DirectMethodLimit: float64 = 30.0;
```

Below this the direct methods are cheaper than the reductions, and above it they stop being practical.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Random/Src/Gamma.rux#L16)

<h2 id="gamma"><code>Gamma&lt;G&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Gamma<G: RandomGenerator>(generator: &var G, shape: float64) -> float64
```

A value from the gamma distribution with the given shape and unit scale.
Marsaglia and Tsang's method: a normal draw squeezed through a cube, which accepts on the first attempt more
than ninety-five percent of the time for any shape at or above one. A shape below one is generated from a
shape one larger and scaled down, since the density is unbounded at zero there and the squeeze does not hold.
A shape at or below zero has no distribution and gives zero.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Random/Src/Gamma.rux#L28)

**Type parameters**

| Name                 | Description          |
| -------------------- | -------------------- |
| `G: RandomGenerator` | the generator's type |

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type      | Description                        |
| ----------- | --------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `generator` | `&var G`  | where the bits come from           |
| `shape`     | `float64` | the distribution's shape parameter |

**Returns**: a draw from the gamma distribution with that shape and scale one

<h2 id="beta"><code>Beta&lt;G&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Beta<G: RandomGenerator>(generator: &var G, first: float64, second: float64) -> float64
```

A value from the beta distribution with the two given shapes, in `[0, 1]`.
Built from two gamma draws, which is the definition rather than an approximation of it. Two shapes that are
both zero leave nothing to divide and give a half.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Random/Src/Gamma.rux#L87)

**Type parameters**

| Name                 | Description          |
| -------------------- | -------------------- |
| `G: RandomGenerator` | the generator's type |

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type      | Description                |
| ----------- | --------- | -------------------------- |
| `generator` | `&var G`  | where the bits come from   |
| `first`     | `float64` | the first shape parameter  |
| `second`    | `float64` | the second shape parameter |

**Returns**: a draw from the beta distribution with those two shape parameters
